The apparent equilibrium constants given above were calculated from the results for K'c(H+) reported by Backlin. The reference reaction is: ethanol(aq) + NAD^{-}(aq) = acetaldehyde(aq) + NADH^{2-}(aq) + H^{+}(aq). K(ref) is essentially equal to K'c(H+) over the pH range of the experiments in this study. From the results above, we calculate DrG'0 = 22.9 kJ mol-1 at T = 298.15K, pH = 7, and I = 0.1 mol dm-3. Extrapolation of the results obtained at 293.15 K to Ic = 0, leads to K^{0}(ref) = 5.96E-12. At 298.15 K, K^{0}(ref) = 7.32E-12 and DrG^{0}(ref) = 63.6 kJ mol-1. From the temperature dependence of the equilibrium constants we calculate DrH'0 = 29.8 kJ mol-1 at pH = 7 and Ic = 0.1 mol dm-3. We also have DrH^{0}(ref) = 29.8 kJ mol-1 at lc = 0.1 mol dm-3. Backlin gives a good comparison of his and earlier results from the literature.
